# Summary of Cairn System Rules

## Pulses
A pulse makes a cairn taller by an amount that depends on both the stride (fixed) and the current height. The formula is: add the stride itself, plus a bonus equal to how many complete strides fit into the current height. The taller the cairn, the bigger each pulse becomes, since more strides fit into a larger number.

## Repeated Pulses
When applying multiple pulses in sequence, you must recalculate the stride count after each pulse using the new height. The count doesn't stay the same—it changes as the cairn grows. This is why later pulses add more marks than earlier ones.

## Leaks
A leak removes marks *after* a pulse, based on the pulsed height (not the starting height). The leak size tells you how many marks must fit into the height for one mark to leak away. Leaks work proportionally—taller cairns lose more marks. The leak eats into the gains from the pulse.

## Drains
A drain is different from a leak because it removes a fixed number of marks every cycle, regardless of height. Over many cycles, as the cairn's height decreases, the pulses get weaker (fewer strides fit into smaller numbers), eventually making the drain larger than each pulse can add. At that point, the cairn shrinks toward zero.

## Origins (Reverse Pulses)
To find the starting height given a final height after pulses, work backwards by undoing each pulse. Test different starting heights to find which one, when pulsed forward, produces the final height. Each cycle requires fresh calculation.

## Merging
When combining two cairns, the result depends on three things: the share of each cairn (proportions that don't sum to 100% of either cairn), and a tether that acts as a multiplier based on the shorter cairn's size. The tether can be positive or negative, adjusting the final height up or down.
